observations: body L1-L5: Schiaparelli's addition begun on p. 262 goes on. The nonagesimal lies in the meridian only when the meridian passes through the pole of the ecliptic, that is when a solstitial point culminates, as said. Its hour angle, computed with Theon's obliquity, reaches at most 0.7 h in the first of Theon's seven climates (latitude 16° 27′), 1.15 h in the third (30° 22′), 1.4 h at 36° and 2.1 h in the seventh (48° 32′): «1 horae vel magis» (L3) and «duas horas attingere potest in climatibus borealioribus» (L13), as printed.

body L6-L14: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the horizon (radius 53.6 pt), the meridian through the pole P and the zenith Z, a straight diameter, the ecliptic from D through M and N to A (radius 101.7 pt) and the hour circle PN (radius 1638 pt), arcs of circles fitted to the print, and the vertical circle ZN, straight; the centre of the horizon lies 1.8 pt below Z. The ecliptic, the circle PN and the line ZN meet in N within 1.4 pt.

body L6-L8: the mark after «parallaxim» (L8) prints as a stop, round and 1.7 pt high, where a comma is expected; those after «ecliptica» (L6) and «reperitur» (L7), also short, have the point of a comma's tail.

body L14-L15: Theon's tables are computed for the Moon at the beginning of each sign (p. 82, L30-L31): in those of Cancer and Capricorn a solstitial point culminates with the Moon, and the nonagesimal is in the meridian.
body L17: the dash before «Ut» measures 10.4 pt.

body L21-L27: the figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the line DA with the hours, two of the evening (vesper) to the left and three of the morning (mane) to the right; the dashed verticals at the hours, their lengths the parallaxes, below the line the negative and above the positive; the curve through their ends, traced from the print, and the Roman figures that number the parallaxes: the smallest is that of the first morning hour (I), and of its neighbours 0 and II that of the hour 0 is the smaller, so X falls between 0 and 1 hour. The dash before «Interdum» (L26) measures 10.1 pt.

body L28-L34: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the line with the hours 0 to 4, the dashed verticals and the curve through their ends, broken in two places as printed, the Roman figures 0, I, II, III, IV and X; here the parallax of the first hour (I) is smaller than that of the meridian (0) and X falls between the first and the second hour. The tables of parallax are in Part II, pp. 95-101 (Part I, p. LXXV, addenda to p. 262), those of the seventh climate on p. 101.

body L32-L37: the rule quoted is p. 84, L12-L15 («Quod cum eveniat, et horae distantiae sint ab ea parte in quam minuta longitudinis desinunt atque prope medium Caelum, minuta longitudinis ... in unum collige»), restated with «in qua». The a of «eveniat» (L35) prints broken.
body L40: the bars of «(+ a) − (− b)» (10.0 and 10.3 pt, as long as the sign of equality) are minus signs.

body L41-L43: «l. 30» is p. 84, L30, the last line of chapter 39; a speck prints after «l.». With the Moon outside the ecliptic its zenith distance differs from that of its degree by up to the latitude, 5°, and a horizontal parallax of 60′ changes by 60′ cos z sin 5°, up to 5′ 14″: «4′ et 5′», as printed. The dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 10.1 pt; a heavy bracket closes Schiaparelli's addition begun on p. 262, L39.
